title: the board's only ship view is the 2.5D voyage: the old flat 2D ship scene, its crew figures, its salute and its board-side cannon audio are removed, the crew roster stays, and the decision-card captain portrait shows the 2.5D voyage's captain
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 the captain said: "the old flat 2D ship view on the board is still there; we do not need it; we only want the 2.5D one". The board renders two ship views at once. (1) The 2.5D voyage (T-125): board/public/game.js mounts the iframe `#voyage-stage` with `/voyage2d/index.html`, built by games/voyage-2d (tools/build.py --live) into the gitignored board/public/voyage2d/. It has its own crew, captain, handoffs, merge salvos and audio (games/voyage-2d/src/board-source.js:27-67, audio2d.js, battleview.js). (2) The old flat 2D ship: `#scene` inside `<section id="shipregion">` (board/public/index.html:251-254), drawn by `SHIP.render` (board/public/ship.js:301-446) with the hull SVG, decks, masts, gun ports, crew figures with name tags and detail cards, handoff flights, the captain figure `#captain`, the ship bar (rate tier, roster toggle, AHOY and order demonstrations, mute), and the Ahoy effects with board-side cannon audio (`enqueue`/`applyEffect`/`nextEffect`/`sound`/`boom`/`unlock`/`silence`, ship.js:733-823). index.html:778 draws the 2D scene whenever the voyage is shown; index.html:208 hides `#scene` only when the voyage is hidden. After this task the voyage is the only ship view.

Remove from board/public/ship.js everything that exists only to draw or animate the 2D scene: RATES/rateFor, ACTIONS/BY_STATE/actionFor, layout/taper, hullSVG, prow, figure, pennant/swatch/vendorMark/bubble/detail as used only by the scene, render, captain, showCard/cards/drag (deck figure detail card, hover, tap and drag), handoffs and its seen/started state, unlock/silence/sound/boom, applyEffect/nextEffect/enqueue, `active`, `muted`, and the constants they alone use. Keep, with unchanged behaviour and output: `hash` (:39), which projectColor (:125) needs (`body` goes, since the portrait now shows the 2.5D image); crewOf (the crew rows from /api/state), roster (sort, group, columns, `rosterOn`, `rosterSort`, `rosterGroup`), portrait (rewritten to the 2.5D image, see the captain decision), patch, esc, prRef, linkPrs, projectColor, vendorColor if roster uses it, and ROLE (crewOf uses it at :226; it stays exported). handoffNotice and HANDOFF_ENDS are removed (their only caller is the removed handoffs(); the voyage imports neither, it has its own src/ship.js) together with their tests, stating that reason, The `module.exports = SHIP` line at :836 STAYS unchanged, because Node tests load it (tests/board-progress.test.sh:141,171, tests/board-identity.test.sh:66, tests/ship.spec.ts:11); of the export list only the `// T-145` handoffNotice/HANDOFF_ENDS entry at :826-827 is removed. The returned SHIP object lists only kept members. ship.js keeps its first-line comment rewritten to say it holds the crew roster, the captain's portrait and shared helpers, and no longer draws a ship.

Captain decision (2026-10-05, on the two trade-offs): (1) the decision-card captain portrait `#capstage` (D-047) stays ONLY as the 2.5D captain: the old 2D voxel portrait drawing (portrait()'s `body({id:'portrait',role:'cap',…})`, ship.js:457-467, and its `.capstage .floor/.glow/.capfig/.fig` rules) is replaced by the 2.5D voyage's own captain art, with no second committed copy of that art; (2) with the voyage closed there is no ship and no merge salute or sound, accepted. How (1) is done: games/voyage-2d/tools/build.py, in its `--live` branch only, after writing board/public/voyage2d/index.html, also writes board/public/voyage2d/captain.webp: the bytes of the baked front-facing whole captain sprite, `bake/sprites.json` → `crew.captain.facings.f.whole.img` (a `data:image/webp;base64,` URI, 401×598; decode the base64), written atomically like index.html (tmp then replace); games/voyage-2d/tools/prepare-board.sh, which today removes `board/public/voyage2d/index.html` after a failed build (:8), also removes `board/public/voyage2d/captain.webp` on that path, so no stale portrait survives a failed build; the voyage cast is unchanged (this is the sprite id `captain`, the human captain, not `firstmate` the handsome young man nor `robot` worker-4). board/public/voyage2d/ is already gitignored, so the image is generated build output, not a repository copy. board/server.ts's static route (about :2088-2089) gains `name.endsWith('.webp') ? 'image/webp'` in its content-type choice; nothing else in board/server.ts changes. portrait() keeps its signature and show/hide behaviour (`host.hidden = !show`, cleared when nothing is pending) but builds `` (aspect 401:598, about 92×137 CSS px inside the existing 184×318 box) plus the existing `.lbl` with `` roleCaptain and `` pose text; whether a Live build exists is the same signal the page already has: game.js is only injected when board/public/voyage2d/index.html exists (board/server.ts:2092), so portrait() adds the `img` only when `window.VOYAGE` is defined; with no Live build the portrait is the label alone and requests nothing under /voyage2d/; if the image still fails to load, the `img` gets `hidden` and only the label shows, never the old 2D figure. Pose: `#capstage[data-pose]` stays the single pose signal (idle/ready/order, as defined in the index.html acceptance item (d) below) and the label text stays capDeciding/capReady/capOrder; ship.css shows the pose on the 2.5D image: idle plain, ready a brass outline glow (`filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px var(--brass))`), order the same glow plus a 6px lift (`transform: translateY(-6px)`), with the lift dropped under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The card layout (portrait box beside the first card, sizes in ship.css:294-308) is unchanged. `body` and `hash` are kept only if something else still uses them (projectColor uses hash; body is removed if portrait no longer uses it).

The roster row keeps every fact the removed deck card showed. Today the card (ship.js:157-189) adds two facts the roster row (ship.js:497-521) lacks: the CI window line (`cwindow`, keys `crewWindow` and `ciNoWindow`, shown only when `c.state === "waiting_ci"`, :172) and the CLI version (`ccli`, key `crewCli`, :185, hidden for a firstmate without a host record exactly like the vendor/model cells). roster()'s job line (`.jb`) gains `ciNoWindow text` when the state is waiting_ci and the row gains a CLI cell `` (value cli_version or crewUnknown) after the model cell. Grid placement (ship.css:403-418, :431-432): the column list gains one `minmax(64px,.7fr)` column after rm and the areas become `"av nm rl pj rv rm rc rd st pr jb"`; `.roster li.rrow .rc{grid-area:rc}` and `.rc` joins the 13px cell rule at :419; the header gains a non-sortable `crewCli label` after the model button so header and rows stay aligned (it is hidden on phones like the other `.rcol`); the phone template's third line becomes `". rv rm rc rc"` (columns unchanged, rv one column, rm one, rc two). The class name is `rc` everywhere. Keys crewWindow, ciNoWindow and crewCli are kept. The project chip moves with it: only when `c.showProject` is true (several projects, as the deck chip used today, ship.js:131,:256) the row's project cell span also carries the class `pchip` and the projectChip title, so a one-project board still has zero `.pchip` (tests/e2e/board-projects.spec.ts:242). The roster row also gains the role mark the deck figure carried: the `
  • ` gains the attribute `data-role="${c.role}"` (fm, w, r, or unknown when the role is not in ROLE), placed after `data-roster` so the class attribute stays exactly `rrow st-${c.state}` and tests/board-progress.test.sh:182-183's `/

board/public/index.html: (a) the crew count against the deck limit that the ship bar showed (`aboard N/limit`, ship.js:364, key `aboard`) moves to the new roster bar as `<span class="aboard">` with the same text and key, so the fact and its zh-CN oracle at tests/e2e/lib/board.ts:12 stay; `#shipregion` keeps only the roster: remove `<div class="scene" id="scene">`; add above the roster a small bar `<div class="rosterbar">` holding the roster toggle `<button class="toggle" id="rosterBtn" aria-controls="roster" aria-pressed=…>` with the same label key `rosterBtn`, the same `board.roster` localStorage key and the same behaviour it has today in the ship bar (ship.js:429-435), so the roster can still be hidden and shown; (b) render() calls `SHIP.crewOf` unconditionally instead of the `window.VOYAGE?.hidden ? crewOf : render(#scene)` split at :778, then `SHIP.roster` as today; (c) remove the `SHIP.captain` call (:781) and the order enqueue in answer() (:899); `observe()` (:432-442) and its `seen`/`initialized` bookkeeping are removed entirely, and its call in render() with it, because the enqueue was its only job (the answer path keeps its own `seen` only if answer() still reads it, otherwise that goes too); (d) pose() no longer reads `#captain` or `SHIP.active()`: the pose is `order` while `sent.size > 0` (a decision is being posted) and for 3.2 seconds after an answer returns with feedback.key one of `recorded`, `customRecorded`, `effectDone`, `mergeRunning` (the old order-effect deadline, timed with a timestamp the answer path sets and a timeout that re-renders), `ready` when `picks.size > 0`, else `idle`; it sets only `#capstage`'s `data-pose` and the `.lbl span` text (`capDeciding/capReady/capOrder`); there is no `.fig` in the portrait any more, so no `c-idle/c-ready/c-order` class is set (index.html:426-428 goes); `changeRequested`, `mergeRefused` and `effectRefused` never give the order pose; (e) the deck wrapper's hidden test at :644 drops `!SHIP.active()`; (f) `SHIP.unlock()` at :872, the pointerdown listener at :1010, the `ship-effect` listener at :1009 (only the removed applyEffect/nextEffect dispatched it, ship.js:808,:815) and `initialized` (:341, used only by observe) are removed; (g) the CSS rule at :208 drops `#scene` and keeps `#capstage` hidden while the voyage is hidden, as today (the portrait's `data-pose` and DOM still update while hidden, which is how tests observe it). The decision deck, the captain's portrait beside the first card (D-047), the lanes, the log, the voyage panel and drawer, and every write path are unchanged.

board/public/ship.css: remove every rule that styles only the removed scene (`.scene` and its descendants, hull, decks, masts, sails, guns, flashes, smoke, sea, crew figures on deck, bubbles/name tags/crew cards on deck, handoff layer, ship bar, ahoy banner, captain-on-deck) and their custom properties and keyframes; keep the roster rules, the captain portrait rules used by `#capstage` — the portrait's 2D figure rules (`.capstage .floor`, `.glow`, `.capfig`, `.capstage[data-pose] .fig.r-cap .tool`, ship.css:299-315) are replaced by `.capstage .capimg` and its three pose rules from the captain decision, while the box and `.lbl` rules (:294-298, :306-308) stay; the on-deck `.captain[data-pose=…]` block (ship.css:195-201) goes with the scene (the `.fig` voxel figure classes the portrait reuses stay if the portrait uses them), and anything index.html still references. Add the `.rosterbar` style (a right-aligned row with the toggle, at least 44px high targets, 13px labels as the ship bar used). tests/board-state.test.sh:292-310 is rewritten: the per-state check asserts `.roster li.st-$st` for every value of `type CrewState` in board/server.ts:127 instead of `.fig.s-$st`, and ship.css gains the missing rule for `st-unknown` (and any other state the roster lacks) so it passes; the `--baseAnim` keyframe loop stays and keeps passing over the kept rules (if no `--baseAnim` remains it asserts that, instead of looping over nothing).

i18n: remove keys whose only users were the removed view (expected: rate1-rate6, ahoyDemo, orderDemo, mute, unmute, crewCard, handoff-only labels) from i18n/ui.en.json and i18n/ui.zh-TW.json together, and only after a grep of board/, games/voyage-2d/src and board/server.ts shows no remaining user (keep a key that any of them still reads, and say so in the PR). Keep `rosterBtn`, `roster*`, `crew*` column labels, `capDeciding`, `capReady`, `capOrder`, `roleCaptain`. tests/i18n.test.sh stays green (every key the page asks for exists, en/zh-TW parity, zh-CN derived through tw2cn.tsv).

In flight and migration. No stored record changes. This is accepted; firstmate runs prepare-board.sh once after the merge, before `fm board`, so the captain sees the 2.5D portrait at once.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check (every bash suite exactly once) and the six gates. No `assert_*` mock names in tests/*.sh (use call_count); new temp dirs use safe_tmpdir.
